science_corp.label: Science Corp SU-8 microwells
science_corp.material: SU-8 microwells coated with poly-D-lysine and laminin
science_corp.measure: Well occupancy, not cell viability. At loading: microwells containing a DAPI-stained nucleus 24 h after loading, in vitro (77 ± 15%, n = 23 scaffolds). At 3 weeks: microwells with neurons expressing fluorescent protein, in vivo (52 ± 23%, n = 13 implants). The two counts use different labels, so they are not a strict survival rate
science_corp.outcome: Neurons extended processes into superficial cortex; some axons were seen throughout the cortical layers
science_corp.status: checked against the preprint text (bioRxiv v1, posted Nov 23, 2024)
science_corp.citation: Brown J. et al. (Science Corporation), Optogenetic stimulation of a cortical biohybrid implant guides goal directed behavior, bioRxiv (2024), doi:10.1101/2024.11.22.624907
evidence: These experiments determined that on average we filled 77±15% (mean ± s.d., n=23 microwell scaffolds, Figure 1d-f). With this loading density, the mean implants contained ~9 x 104 neurons.
At this time point, we found 52±23% (mean±s.d.) of microwells to be loaded with neurons expressing fluorescent protein (n=13 implants, Figure 2b-c, e).
engrafted neurons extended extensive processes into the superficial layers of cortex
we were able to observe axons throughout the layers of the cerebral cortex
0.1 mg/mL poly-d-Lysine (Gibco) and 0.1 mg/mL Laminin (Millipore Sigma, L2020)
